terms.comment: The everyday greeting of Plautus and Terence (Lewis & Short: “very freq. and class.”).

terms.gloss: hello, be well (to a man; to a woman)

evidence: Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.16.4; Mart. 3.95.1 (Lewis & Short s.v. aveō)
terms.comment: More formal than salvē: in Martial the morning greeting, and the Avē of the Vulgate (Luc. 1.28). Lewis & Short doubts that Cicero used it.

phrases.latin: Ō Syre noster, salvē: quid fit? quid agitur? — Rēctē. — Optimē est.
phrases.english: Hello, Syrus my friend: how’s it going? how are things? — Fine. — Splendid.

phrases.latin: ut lībertī servīque māne salvēre, vesperī valēre sibi singulī dīcerent
phrases.english: that each of his freedmen and slaves should say hello to him in the morning and goodbye in the evening

phrases.latin: Salvē, adulēscēns. — Et tū multum salvētō, adulēscentula.
phrases.english: Hello, young man. — And a very good day to you, young lady.

sources: Lewis & Short: salveo · Lewis & Short: salvus · Lewis & Short: aveo
